general_rules.rule: ✅ Write `border` (or `border-t`, `border-b`…): the width comes from the `border-width.default` token
✅ Remove a border with `border-0` / `border-t-0` — a reset to zero is not a value
✅ Add a `border-width.*` token named after its role when a component genuinely needs another width
❌ Never hard-code a width: `border-2`, `border-[1.5px]`, `border-(length:3px)` — `npm run tokens:lint-values` rejects them
❌ Do not use `border-none` to remove a border: it sets the border **style**, not its width
✅ Write the mobile version without a prefix, then add `sm:` / `md:` / `lg:` for wider screens
✅ Pick the first breakpoint at which the layout breaks, not a specific device
❌ Never write an arbitrary breakpoint (`min-[600px]:`, `max-[900px]:`) — only the prefixes in the table exist
❌ Never read `var(--breakpoint-*)` inside a media query: media queries do not resolve variables
❌ Do not change a `breakpoint.*` value without declaring the same value, as a literal, in the `@theme` of `styles/globals.css` — the bridge lint will remind you
✅ `background.default` — the background of `<html>` and of root containers.
❌ Do not use `background.default` for cards — use `background.subtle`.
✅ `background.elevated` for anything that floats above the content (a menu, a dialog).
❌ Do not use `background.elevated` for an inline card — it is not a floating surface.
✅ `text.subtle` for field labels, visible placeholders, metadata.
❌ Do not dim `text.default` with opacity to fake `text.subtle` — use the dedicated token.
✅ `text.action.on` only on a `color.action.background.default` background.
❌ Do not use `text.destructive.default` for warnings — it is reserved for errors.

✅ `text.destructive.default` for every destructive label, including on a `bg-destructive/10`–`/30` tint: it is darker than the error fill in light mode and lighter in dark mode, so it stays at 4.5:1 or more on the page, a card and a popover.
✅ `border.input` for every `<input>`, `<select>` and `<textarea>` border.
❌ Do not use `border.focus` at rest or on hover — only for the `:focus-visible` state.
✅ `border.subtle` for dividers between the sections of a page.
❌ Do not mix `border.default` and `border.subtle` in the same component.
✅ `icon.action` only inside a primary button or an action badge.
❌ Do not use `icon.default` for an icon inside a primary button — use `icon.action`.
✅ Always pair `action.background.default` with `action.background.foreground` for the text.
❌ Do not use these tokens for the `secondary`, `ghost` or `outline` variants.
✅ Use `feedback.error.default` for the borders and rings of invalid fields and for the `bg-destructive/10`–`/30` tints.
❌ Do not use `feedback.error.default` for text or icons: on a card it drops to 4.28:1, and to 3.00:1 on a card under a 20% tint. Text goes through `text.destructive.default` (`text-destructive`).
✅ On a solid error background, always use `color.feedback.error.foreground` (shadcn alias `--destructive-foreground`).
❌ Do not use them for warnings or successes — dedicated tokens will be added.
❌ Never put hard-coded white on an error surface: in dark mode, white on red.500 drops to 2.89:1.
✅ Unordered categories: `chart-1` to `chart-5`, in order, skipping none.
✅ Back every color up with a label or a legend: color alone never carries meaning.
✅ Ordered data: `color.chart.sequential.*`, from lightest (low value) to darkest.
❌ Never use the sequential palette for categories: its steps blur together.
❌ Do not use a series color for text or for a state (positive, negative): these are not feedback colors.
✅ `bg-black/10` for a modal's scrim: it darkens the same way in both modes.
❌ Do not use `static.*` for a regular surface or text: dark mode would not apply — use `background.*` / `text.*`.
**Always use the semantic tokens** — never the `mist.X` or `violet.X` primitive values directly in components. Primitives are private (`--ds-prim-*`).
**Never fake subtlety with opacity** — use `color.text.subtle`, not `color.text.default` with `opacity-50`.
**Follow the surface hierarchy**: `default` → `subtle` → `elevated`. A card is `subtle`, a popover is `elevated`.
**Always test both modes** — every component must be checked in light AND dark before it ships.
**Accessibility first** — the minimum contrast ratio is 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) for body text, and 3:1 for large text and UI components.

**Contrast is checked mechanically** — `npm run tokens:lint-contrast` (part of `npm run tokens-validate`) resolves every background / text pair the system actually ships, in both modes, and fails below the threshold. The pairs under watch are declared in `scripts/lint-contrast.ts`: **add a pair as soon as a new background / text combination appears in the system**, otherwise nothing covers it. A pair is checked as it renders: a `bg-<role>/<n>` tint is composited onto each surface it can sit on (page, card, popover), in each state (rest, hover, focus), before the ratio is measured. Fix the token, never the threshold.
✅ Read every default string from `UI_STRINGS`, never as a literal in the JSX
✅ Expose an override prop for every string a component renders
✅ Write the defaults in English; supply the other locales through props
❌ Never hard-code an `aria-label`, a `title` or `sr-only` text in a component
❌ Never mix two languages in the defaults — `npm run index:strings` fails on any literal
**Follow the hierarchy** — elevation must reflect the surface's real position on the Z axis. A popover never has less elevation than an inline card.
**Always test in dark mode** — light-mode shadows vanish in dark mode unless adjusted. The tokens handle this automatically.
**Elevation transitions** — use `transition-shadow` with `duration-normal` (200ms) on state changes (hover, focus).
**`shadow-inner` stands alone** — never pair it with an outer shadow on the same element.
**No decorative shadows** — elevation expresses structure, not style. Do not add `shadow-lg` to a card just to make it look nice.

**Never hard-code a ring width on a focus state** — `ring-1`, `ring-2` and `ring-3` are pixels, forbidden by the repository's first rule. The linter rejects them under any `focus`, `focus-visible`, `focus-within`, `data-[active=true]`, `data-[focused=true]` or `aria-invalid` prefix.

**Never `outline-none`** — use `FOCUS_OUTLINE_RESET` (`outline-hidden`). In forced-colors mode, `box-shadow`s are not painted: `outline-none` leaves the element with no indicator at all, whereas `outline-hidden` keeps a transparent outline that the mode makes visible. On top of that, `outline-none` poisons `--tw-outline-style`, which silently disabled the `outline-1` of ScrollArea and NavigationMenu.

**The invalid-state ring follows the focus ring's width** — both can apply at once on a field that is invalid and focused. Two different widths give a result that depends on the order of the utilities in the compiled stylesheet.

**A bare `ring-0` is a legitimate removal** — it is how a wrapper such as InputGroup takes over the indicator of its inner control. Under a focus state (`focus-visible:ring-0`) it removes the indicator, and counts as a reset under rule 5.

**Hiding the outline requires drawing a ring — checked occurrence by occurrence, and target by target.** The ring must appear in the _same_ class string, on the _same_ target: a reset written under `**:`, `*:`, `[&_x]:` or `before:` hides the indicator of other nodes, and only a ring under the same variant answers it. A component that neutralizes the outline in ten places and draws a ring in one does not meet the rule, and neither did NavigationMenu, whose `**:data-[slot=navigation-menu-link]:focus:outline-none` hid every link's ring while the menu drew its own.
**A universal starting point** — `motion.duration.normal` (200ms) with `motion.easing.default` is the default combination for any new transition.
**Always use the CSS tokens** — never hard-code a duration or an easing in the code.
**`ease-in` for exits, `ease-out` for entrances** — a universal UX convention that matches natural physical motion.
**`ease-spring` sparingly** — only for expressive, deliberate interactions (positive feedback, gamification). Never on basic state transitions.
**Never work around the tokens** — no hard-coded values and no `!important` on transition properties.
✅ The token, under the state's variant
❌ Same rendering, but the token is gone: ESLint rejects it
❌ Hard-coded value
✅ Through Tailwind
✅ Through CSS
✅ Modal backdrop
**Three cases, three tokens** — `disabled`, `placeholder` and `overlay` are the only legitimate contexts for global opacity.

**A disabled state is written `opacity-disabled`** under its variant (`disabled:opacity-disabled`) — never `opacity-50`, which ESLint rejects: the value is the token's, not a step of Tailwind's scale.
**Never use opacity to fake a subtle color** — always use `color.text.subtle` / `text-muted-foreground`.
**Opacity is not selective** — it applies to the whole DOM subtree. When only part of it should change, use targeted color tokens.
**`opacity.overlay` at `0.8` is the reference value** — do not lower it for standard modals: it hurts the readability of the main content.
✅ Standard card
✅ Default button
✅ Pill badge
✅ Table cell — no radius
✅ Modal
**Always use the tokens** — no arbitrary values such as `rounded-[7px]`. When no token fits, escalate to the design team.
**Consistency within a component** — every corner of a component uses the same token, unless there is a stated reason (an element that attaches to an edge of the screen, for example).
**`radius.lg` is shadcn's default** — it is the starting point for any card-like component.
**`radius.full` only for pill shapes** — avatars, toggles, rounded badges. Do not use it on standard buttons.
**`radius.none` is a deliberate choice** — use it only for full-bleed components or data-grid elements, not as a default.
**Two axes, two vocabularies** — `space.component.*` inside components; `space.layout.*` for the overall layout. Never swap them.
**No arbitrary values** — use the tokens only. When an in-between value is needed, discuss it with the design team first.
**Stay on the component axis** — a form uses `lg` (24px) between its fields and `md` (16px) for inner padding. Keep to that axis throughout the same component.
**`page-padding` is applied once** — on the page's root container, not on each section.
**`content-*` through `max-width`** — these tokens set maximum widths, not padding. Always pair them with `mx-auto` to center.
**JetBrains Mono is the default typeface** — never override `font-family` on standard UI components without design approval.
**Always pair `size` with `lineHeight`** — a heading without `leading-tight` looks too loose; body text without `leading-normal` is hard to read.
**`tracking-tight` only from `text-3xl` up** — on small text, negative spacing hurts readability.
**`tracking-wider` is for all-caps only** — never use it on regular lowercase text.
**A strict weight hierarchy** — `normal` → body, `medium` → labels and navigation, `semibold` → subheadings, `bold` → main headings. Do not skip levels.

Accordion: **MUST NOT** — hold critical content that has to stay visible at all times
**MUST NOT** — nest an `Accordion` inside another: one level only
**MUST** — give each trigger explicit text, never an icon alone
**Note** — a disabled trigger drops pointer events and applies `opacity-disabled`
**MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation → use `NavigationMenu` or `Tabs`
Alert: **MUST NOT** — show a transient message (toast) → use `Sonner`
**MUST NOT** — act as a blocking dialog → use `AlertDialog`
**MUST NOT** — place more than one `Alert` per page section
**MUST NOT** — add a second `role="alert"` among the children: the root already carries it
**MUST NOT** — put variable-width content in `AlertAction`, which is absolutely positioned at the top right
AlertDialog: **MUST NOT** — carry a plain informational message → use `Dialog`, or `Sonner` for a notification
**MUST NOT** — open an `AlertDialog` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST NOT** — re-implement the focus trap: Radix provides it
**MUST** — render an `AlertDialogTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
AspectRatio: **MUST NOT** — hold free-flowing text: it would be clipped or overflow
**MUST** — fill the frame with an `absolute` child (`size-full`) or an `object-cover` media element
**MUST** — pass a single direct child; wrap several elements in a container
Avatar: **MUST** — provide an `AvatarFallback`, shown when the image is missing
**MUST NOT** — use `AvatarBadge` without an `aria-label` that says what it signals
**MUST NOT** — show more than 4 avatars in an `AvatarGroup`: beyond that, show the first 3 and put the rest in `AvatarGroupCount`
Badge: **MUST NOT** — act as an action button → use `Button` with `size="xs"`
**MUST NOT** — exceed three words of text
**MUST** — keep the `destructive` variant for error or critical-alert statuses
**MUST** — check the contrast of the background-less `ghost` and `link` variants on every surface they appear on
Breadcrumb: **MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation: it is a contextual landmark
**MUST** — place a single `Breadcrumb` per page, at the top of the main content
**MUST NOT** — make the last item (`BreadcrumbPage`) clickable
**Note** — separators and the ellipsis are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`)
**MUST NOT** — replace the root's `aria-label="breadcrumb"`, **unless** to translate it
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the `UI_STRINGS.breadcrumb` strings (`srLabel` on `BreadcrumbEllipsis`)
Button: **MUST NOT** — render a `<button>` to navigate to an external site → an `<a href>`, through `asChild` to keep the look
**MUST NOT** — place more than 2 `variant="default"` (primary) buttons in the same view
**MUST NOT** — convey a state through color alone: add text or a tooltip
**MUST NOT** — nest a `<button>` inside another, including through `asChild`
ButtonGroup: **MUST NOT** — group unrelated actions → just space them out (`flex gap-*`)
**MUST** — only hold children whose borders can merge: the inner corners are removed
Calendar: **MUST NOT** — serve as a scheduler or planner (day or week views): the design system does not provide one
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Calendar` per view, **unless** comparing two date ranges
**MUST** — place the `Calendar` inside a container (`Popover`, `Card`…): it does not position itself
**MUST NOT** — break keyboard navigation (arrows between days, Tab to the controls)
Card: **MUST NOT** — nest `Card`s more than one level deep: show hierarchy with a different background
**MUST NOT** — put long content in `CardAction`, which sits at the top right of the header
**MUST NOT** — place more than 2 actions in `CardFooter`
**MUST NOT** — put `onClick` on a `Card`: wrap it in an `<a>` or a `<button>` when it is clickable
Carousel: **MUST NOT** — hold critical content that must be visible without interaction → use a grid
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Carousel` per view: their keyboard navigation conflicts
**MUST NOT** — hide the previous and next buttons
**MUST** — contain a `CarouselContent` and at least one `CarouselItem`
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the `UI_STRINGS.carousel` strings (`srLabel` on `CarouselPrevious` and `CarouselNext`)
Chart: **MUST NOT** — present raw data meant to be read value by value → use `Table`
**MUST** — pass `ChartContainer` a `config` with at least one entry
**MUST** — read a series' color from the `--color-<key>` variable that `ChartStyle` injects for each `config` key (`fill="var(--color-revenue)"`); it is not a token: its value comes from `config`
**MUST NOT** — nest `ChartContainer`s: one container per chart
**MUST** — pair the chart with alternative text or a data table: screen readers do not read the SVG
Checkbox: **MUST** — pair the checkbox with a visible label: `Label` (`id` / `htmlFor`), or `Field` with a `FieldLabel`; inside a `Field` as soon as it has a description or an error message (`rule-09`)
**MUST NOT** — serve mutually exclusive choices → use `RadioGroup`
**MUST NOT** — let the enlarged hit area (`after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2`) overlap a neighboring control
**Note** — a disabled checkbox is not submitted with the native form
**MUST NOT** — convey a state through color alone: add an icon or text
Collapsible: **MUST NOT** — serve as multi-level navigation → use `Accordion`
**MUST** — make the trigger recognizable as interactive (a button or a link)
**MUST NOT** — hide content the page needs to be understood at a glance
**MUST NOT** — manage `aria-expanded` yourself: Radix does it
Combobox: **MUST NOT** — be used for 15 options or fewer without search → `RadioGroup` up to 5, `Select` or `NativeSelect` from 6 to 15 (`rule-20`)
**MUST** — render a `ComboboxEmpty` for the "no results" case
**MUST** — in multiple selection, provide an `anchor` (`useComboboxAnchor`) so the popup opens below the chips
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component

**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the accessible names of the three icon-only buttons (trigger, clear, chip remove) through `triggerLabel`, `clearLabel` and `removeLabel`: they default to the English `UI_STRINGS.combobox`
**MUST** — pass `removeLabel` to a `ComboboxChip` whose children are not the item's text: the default name is built from the chip's rendered text, so each remove button says which item it removes
Command: **MUST NOT** — serve as a plain search field → an `Input` that filters the list
**MUST** — render a `CommandEmpty` for the "no results" case
**MUST** — wire up the keyboard shortcut that `CommandShortcut` displays yourself: it is only a label
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
**MUST** — in dialog mode, set `title` and `description`: rendered `sr-only`, they name the dialog
ContextMenu: **MUST NOT** — serve as the main navigation menu → use `DropdownMenu`
**MUST** — only offer actions that belong to the targeted element: the menu replaces the browser's own
**Note** — only one context menu opens at a time (Radix handles it)
**MUST** — make the same actions reachable from the keyboard (`Shift+F10` or the Menu key)
Dialog: **MUST NOT** — carry a destructive confirmation → use `AlertDialog`
**MUST NOT** — open a `Dialog` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST** — render a `DialogTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
**MUST NOT** — hold content that needs its own scrolling → `Sheet` from `md` up, `Drawer` below (`rule-21`), or a dedicated page
**MUST** — keep a way to close the dialog when `showCloseButton={false}` hides the button
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate `UI_STRINGS.dialog` through `closeLabel`
Direction: **MUST** — place the `DirectionProvider` above every Radix component that reads the direction
**MUST** — keep the `dir` attribute of `<html>` consistent with the `DirectionProvider`, which does not replace it
**Note** — a utility component: it renders nothing visible

**Note** — **The only component in the system without a `data-slot`**: it renders no DOM node of its own, so no element can carry the attribute. The exception is declared in the code with `// no-data-slot:` and checked by `npm run index:data-slot`. Target the direction through the `dir` attribute Radix sets on the consuming components
Drawer: **MUST NOT** — be used on desktop (`md` and up) → use `Dialog` or `Sheet`
**MUST NOT** — exceed 80vh in height in the `top` or `bottom` direction (applied by default)
**MUST NOT** — open a `Drawer` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST** — render a `DrawerTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
**MUST** — test a `Drawer` with scrolling content on mobile: the close gesture can capture the scroll
DropdownMenu: **MUST NOT** — serve as a right-click context menu → use `ContextMenu`
**MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation → use `NavigationMenu`
**Note** — only one `DropdownMenu` opens at a time (Radix handles it)
**Note** — the content takes the trigger's width by default (`w-(--radix-dropdown-menu-trigger-width)`)
Empty: **MUST NOT** — report a server error → use an `Alert` with `variant="destructive"`
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Empty` per view
**MUST NOT** — put essential information in `EmptyMedia`: the media is decorative
**MUST NOT** — exceed two sentences of description; frame it around the action to take

**MUST** — `EmptyTitle` renders an `<h2>`: pass `as` (`"h3"`…) to follow the page's hierarchy — one level below the heading of the section that holds the empty state. Do not style through `as`: the look is fixed
Field: **MUST NOT** — nest `FieldSet`s more than 2 levels deep
**MUST** — set `data-invalid` yourself, from the validation result (server or client): `Field` validates nothing
**MUST** — set `aria-invalid` on the control itself: `Field` does not pass it down
**MUST NOT** — use `orientation="horizontal"` in a layout that has to fit on mobile → `orientation="responsive"`, which switches to a row once its `FieldGroup` is wide enough
**MUST** — place a `Field` with `orientation="responsive"` inside a `FieldGroup`, whose width it reads (`@container/field-group`)
**Note** — `FieldError` renders nothing without `children` or a non-empty `errors`
**MUST** — use `FieldLabel` to tie a label to a control (`htmlFor`): `FieldTitle` is not a `<label>`
Heading: **MUST NOT** — skip a heading level (an `h3` under an `h1`)
**MUST NOT** — place more than one `h1` per page
**MUST** — only use `as` when the semantic level differs from the visual level
**MUST NOT** — style a heading by hand: go through `level`
HoverCard: **MUST NOT** — contain interactive elements (forms, buttons) → use `Popover`
**MUST NOT** — be the only path on mobile, where hover does not exist: provide access on tap
**MUST NOT** — hold information the user cannot do without: its content is a supplement
**MUST NOT** — sit on two adjacent triggers (a dense list): hovering one opens the other
**MUST NOT** — hold critical content the user has to see
Illustration: **MUST** — provide a descriptive `alt`: it feeds `role="img"` and `aria-label`
**MUST** — replace this placeholder with real illustrations before production
**MUST NOT** — display a content image → use `` or `next/image`
**MUST** — set the dimensions through `className`: the container imposes none
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the default alternative text (`UI_STRINGS.illustration`) through `alt`
Input: **MUST NOT** — offer a choice among fixed values → use `Select` or `Checkbox`
**MUST NOT** — replace a visible `Label` with a `placeholder`
**MUST NOT** — set `autoFocus` on more than one field per view
**Note** — when disabled, the field shows the `not-allowed` cursor and its value is not submitted
InputGroup: **MUST NOT** — be used without an `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea` as a direct child
**MUST NOT** — mix `block-*` and `inline-*` add-ons in the same group: `block-*` add-ons switch the layout to a column
**MUST** — set `disabled` on the child field: the group only mirrors its appearance (`has-disabled`)
**MUST** — use `InputGroupButton` for a button inside an add-on
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
InputOtp: **MUST NOT** — take free text or more than 8 characters: it is meant for codes of 4 to 8 characters
**MUST** — give each `InputOTPSlot` the `index` of its position
**Note** — `spellCheck` is off by default: the browser offers no correction on a code
**MUST NOT** — redefine the ARIA roles: the `input-otp` library handles them
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
Item: **MUST** — keep the `xs` size for context menus, never a main list
**MUST NOT** — place more than 3 actions in `ItemActions`

**MUST** — place each `Item` of an `ItemGroup` as a direct child (or through `.map()`): `ItemGroup` gives it `role="listitem"`. An `Item` rendered by an intermediate component is not detected — pass it `role="listitem"` explicitly
Kbd: **MUST NOT** — stand for anything but a keyboard key
**MUST NOT** — add a click handler: the component is not interactive (`pointer-events-none`)
**MUST** — check the contrast in the dark theme, on the actual background
**MUST** — pair a symbol key (⌘, ⇧) with a text label for screen readers
Label: **MUST NOT** — replace a `Label` with a `placeholder`
**MUST** — tie every `Label` to its control (`htmlFor` or `aria-labelledby`); no field goes without a visible label
**MUST NOT** — serve as a section title → use `FieldLegend` or `Heading`
**MUST NOT** — tie more than one `Label` to a control
Logo: **MUST** — show the logo through the `Logo` component, never through a hand-inserted SVG
**MUST NOT** — distort its proportions: go through `size`
**MUST** — place the brand name next to the `Logo`: it does not render its children
**MUST** — replace this placeholder with the real brand assets as soon as they exist
Menubar: **MUST NOT** — serve as site navigation → use `NavigationMenu`
**MUST NOT** — nest submenus more than 2 levels deep
**Note** — a `disabled` item is dimmed (`opacity-disabled`) and inert (`pointer-events-none`)
**MUST** — wire a real handler for every shortcut `MenubarShortcut` displays
NativeSelect: **MUST NOT** — be used when the list has to be filtered by typing → use `Combobox`
**Note** — the open menu is drawn by the browser and cannot be styled
**Note** — the options take the system colors (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`)
**Note** — `size` is a prop of the component, not the native `<select>` attribute: `"sm"` or `"default"`
**MUST** — provide an empty `<option value="">` as a placeholder
NavigationMenu: **MUST NOT** — serve as a menu of actions (commands) → use `Menubar` or `DropdownMenu`
**Note** — `viewport={false}` renders the content inline, without a viewport
**MUST** — render every link with `NavigationMenuLink`, which handles `data-active`
**MUST** — give the parent of `NavigationMenuIndicator` relative positioning
Pagination: **MUST NOT** — serve as hierarchical navigation → use `Breadcrumb`
**MUST** — manage the pagination state and URLs yourself: the component holds none
**MUST NOT** — duplicate `aria-current="page"`, which the active page already carries
**MUST** — give `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` a valid `href` or a handler
**Note** — the ellipsis is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`)
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate `UI_STRINGS.pagination` through `text`, `label` and `srLabel`
PasswordInput: **MUST** — wrap it in a `Field` with its `FieldLabel`
**MUST NOT** — be used for non-sensitive text → use `Input`
**MUST NOT** — pass `type`: the component controls it
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the toggle's labels (`UI_STRINGS.passwordInput`)
Popover: **MUST NOT** — show plain help text → use `Tooltip` or `HoverCard`
**MUST** — set `as` on `PopoverTitle` from the real hierarchy: it renders an `<h2>` by default, `as="h3"` under an `h2` section
**MUST NOT** — show a list of actions → use `DropdownMenu`
**Note** — only one `Popover` opens at a time, unless the state is controlled by hand
**MUST NOT** — hold content that needs its own scrolling, or a form of more than 3 fields → use `Dialog` or `Sheet`
**MUST** — test the positioning near the edges of the screen (Radix flips it automatically)
Progress: **MUST NOT** — show indeterminate progress without saying so: set `aria-valuetext` or an explicit label
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Progress` bar per section
**MUST** — name the bar (`aria-label` or a tied `<label>`)
**MUST** — keep `value` between 0 and `max` (100 by default): out-of-range values are not handled
**MUST NOT** — serve as a data gauge (temperature, stock…): `Progress` expresses how far a task has gone
RadioGroup: **MUST NOT** — be used for more than 5 options → `Select` from 6 to 15, `Combobox` beyond (`rule-20`)
**MUST** — tie each `RadioGroupItem` to a `Label`, and place the group in a `Field` as soon as it has a description or an error message (`rule-09`)
**MUST NOT** — add padding to enlarge the hit area: it is already enlarged (`after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2`)
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
Resizable: **MUST NOT** — serve a fixed-width layout → a CSS grid (`grid`)
**MUST** — give each `ResizablePanel` a `minSize`, so its content is never crushed
**MUST NOT** — take away the `ResizableHandle`'s focus or its arrow-key control
**MUST NOT** — nest `ResizablePanelGroup`s more than 2 levels deep
**MUST NOT** — mix `vertical` and `horizontal` orientations at the same level
ScrollArea: **MUST NOT** — handle the page's main scrolling: let the `<body>` scroll
**MUST** — give the parent a defined height (fixed or flex), otherwise nothing scrolls
**MUST NOT** — make focusable content in the area unreachable from the keyboard
Select: **MUST NOT** — be used when the list has to be filtered by typing → use `Combobox`
**MUST NOT** — be used below `md` when the options need no rich rendering → `NativeSelect` (`rule-20`)
**MUST** — account for the `Portal` in stacking (`z-index`): the content renders outside its parent
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
Separator: **MUST** — keep `decorative` (the default) for a purely visual separator: it is hidden from screen readers
**MUST** — only pass `decorative={false}` when the separation carries meaning (two distinct sections of an article)
**MUST** — separate with spacing (`gap`) when a separator adds no meaning
Sheet: **MUST NOT** — carry a short confirmation → use `AlertDialog` or `Dialog`
**MUST NOT** — open a `Sheet` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST** — render a `SheetTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
**Note** — on the left and right sides, the width is capped at `sm:max-w-sm`
**MUST** — keep a way to close the panel when `showCloseButton={false}` hides the button
**MUST NOT** — be used below `md` → `Drawer`, **unless** it is side navigation (`rule-21`)
**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate `UI_STRINGS.sheet` through `closeLabel`
Sidebar: **MUST NOT** — place more than one `Sidebar` per side in the same `SidebarProvider`
**MUST** — check that a nested layout copes with the margins and shadows of the `floating` and `inset` variants
**MUST** — give a `tooltip` to every `SidebarMenuButton` collapsed to its icon
**MUST NOT** — bind `Ctrl+B` / `⌘+B` to another action: `SidebarProvider` registers it to collapse the bar

**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the strings the sidebar renders for screen readers: `toggleLabel` on `SidebarTrigger` and `SidebarRail`, `mobileTitle` and `mobileDescription` on `Sidebar` (defaults in `UI_STRINGS.sidebar`)
Skeleton: **MUST NOT** — stay on screen once the content has loaded
**MUST** — match the final content's dimensions (height, width, radius), so its arrival does not shift the layout
**MUST NOT** — animate a skeleton while `prefers-reduced-motion` is on
**MUST NOT** — show more skeletons than the entries expected: each one holds the place of content that is coming
Slider: **MUST NOT** — be used to enter an exact value → a `number` `Input`

**MUST** — always name the Slider: `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing to the `id` of a `<Label>` (`htmlFor` does not name a thumb, which is not a form field). With several thumbs, name each one as well through `thumbLabels` ("Minimum price", "Maximum price")
**MUST** — give a vertical `Slider` a minimum height (`min-h-40`)
**MUST** — pick `min`, `max` and `step` so that `max - min` is a multiple of `step`
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
Sonner: **MUST NOT** — carry a critical message that requires an action → use `AlertDialog`
**MUST** — place a single `<Toaster />`, at the root of the layout
**MUST NOT** — show more than 3 toasts at once
Spinner: **MUST** — replace the default `aria-label` (`"Loading"`) with a label that describes the action ("Signing in")
**MUST NOT** — show more than one `Spinner` in the same area: one indicator
**Note** — the size is set through `className` (`size-3`, `size-6`): there is no `size` prop
**MUST NOT** — signal a load that lasts more than 10 s → use `Progress` with a percentage
**MUST NOT** — add a second `role="status"` in the parent: the component carries it
**MUST** — the default accessible name comes from `UI_STRINGS.spinner`, in English — override it through `aria-label`
Switch: **MUST NOT** — serve a choice between two named options → use `RadioGroup`
**MUST** — pair it with a visible label: `Label` (`htmlFor`), or `Field` with a `FieldLabel`; inside a `Field` as soon as it has a description or an error message (`rule-09`)
**MUST NOT** — add padding to enlarge the hit area: it is already enlarged (`after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2`)
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
Table: **MUST NOT** — be used for layout: it is for tabular data only
**MUST NOT** — add horizontal scrolling on a parent: the container already scrolls (`overflow-x-auto`)
**MUST** — beyond 4 columns, hide the secondary columns below 640 px (the `Table` container already scrolls horizontally)
**MUST** — name the table (`TableCaption` or `aria-label`) when the context does not
Tabs: **MUST NOT** — serve as navigation between separate pages → use `NavigationMenu`
**MUST NOT** — be used when several sections must be visible together → use `Accordion` (`Tabs` shows only one)
**Note** — a `disabled` trigger stops receiving pointer events and takes `opacity-disabled`
**MUST NOT** — make a panel's content depend on another tab
Textarea: **Note** — the field grows with its content (`field-sizing-content`); set a fixed height through `className`
**MUST NOT** — redefine the background without its dark counterpart (`dark:bg-input/30` by default)
**Note** — a server component: it renders without `"use client"`
Toggle: **MUST NOT** — trigger an action that cannot be undone → use `Button`
**MUST NOT** — stand in for a `Switch` in a settings form
**MUST NOT** — combine the `outline` variant with a border on the parent
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component
ToggleGroup: **MUST** — pass `type="single"` for an exclusive selection, `type="multiple"` otherwise
**MUST** — give the `ToggleGroup` an `aria-label` that describes the group
**MUST NOT** — serve as navigation → use `Tabs` or `NavigationMenu`
**Note** — `spacing={0}` (the default) merges the borders; above that, the items are spaced out
**MUST NOT** — redefine `variant` or `size` on a `ToggleGroupItem`, **unless** to set one item apart: the group passes them down
Tooltip: **MUST NOT** — contain interactive elements (links, buttons) → use `Popover`
**MUST NOT** — exceed one line or 80 characters of text
**MUST NOT** — be the only place critical information appears
**MUST** — place a `TooltipProvider` higher in the tree, for example in the root layout
**MUST NOT** — sit directly on a `disabled` element, which receives neither focus nor hover: wrap the element in a `<span tabIndex={0}>` that carries the trigger

composition_rules.rule: Use only Semantic tokens (--color-*, --space-*, --elevation-*, --motion-*, --radius-*, --zindex-*) and Component aliases (--background, --primary, etc.) in component code. Never reference Primitive tokens (--ds-prim-*) directly.

Never use raw values (oklch, hex, rgb, px, rem, ms, cubic-bezier) in component files. Every visual value must trace to a token. Exception: CSS attribute selectors targeting third-party library SVG attributes (annotate with // allow-raw: <reason>).
All class name composition must use cn() from @/lib/utils. Inline conditional className strings are not permitted.
Component variants must be declared with cva() from class-variance-authority. Use data-variant and data-size attributes to expose variant state for CSS targeting.
Icons must come exclusively from @phosphor-icons/react. No other icon library may be used. Default icon size within components is size-4 (1rem).
TooltipProvider must wrap the entire application at the layout root. Do not instantiate Tooltip outside of a TooltipProvider.
Sonner Toaster must be instantiated once at the layout root. Do not render multiple Toaster instances.

Dialog, Sheet, AlertDialog, and Drawer must always include an accessible title element (DialogTitle, SheetTitle, AlertDialogTitle, DrawerTitle). Visually-hidden titles are acceptable for screen-reader-only labels.

Every form control (Input, Textarea, Select, NativeSelect, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch) MUST have an associated visible label: Field with FieldLabel, or Label through htmlFor. It MUST sit in a Field as soon as it carries a description or an error message, which Field lays out and links to the control.
Components using asChild must pass a single React element as children. The child receives all props via Slot.Root — do not wrap it in an additional element.
Dark mode is class-based (.dark). Never use prefers-color-scheme media queries in component code — theming is controlled by ThemeProvider at the root.

Spacing between components must use Semantic space tokens: space-component-xs/sm/md/lg/xl for intra-component gaps, space-layout-page-padding for page edges, space-layout-section-gap for section breaks.
All new components must expose a data-slot attribute on the root element whose value matches the component name (e.g., data-slot='button'). Sub-parts also carry data-slot for CSS targeting.
Beta components (status: beta in design-system.index.json) may have breaking API changes. Do not use them in production flows without explicit sign-off.

Run npm run tokens-validate before every commit. Zero errors are required to merge. If a needed Semantic token does not exist, open a GitHub issue labeled design-system instead of creating an ad-hoc token.

Dark mode is the .dark class on <html>, set by ThemeProvider (next-themes). It follows the OS preference by default (defaultTheme="system") by setting that class, never through a prefers-color-scheme media query. Never override mode token values inline.

Sidebar tokens follow the naming pattern color.sidebar.<role>.<emphasis>. Use --color-sidebar-primary (active item bg), --color-sidebar-primary-on (text on active), --color-sidebar-accent-default (hover surface), --color-sidebar-accent-foreground (text on hover). Do not use the legacy flat names.

The canonical size scale is xs | sm | default | lg, with the square-format series icon-xs | icon-sm | icon | icon-lg. MUST use only the sizes listed in the component's inventory entry: a component that omits a step does not accept it, and no component accepts a name outside the scale. Components with no sizes field take no size prop.

A `variant` prop carries exactly one axis: appearance, intent, or media. MUST NOT assume a component accepts a value because a sibling does. Media values (icon, image) belong to *Media sub-components only. MUST use variant="destructive" for irreversible actions, never to obtain red styling.

Pick the selection control from the number of options and the screen width. One value out of 2 to 5 options: `RadioGroup`, with every option visible. Out of 6 to 15: `Select` from `md` up; below `md`, `NativeSelect`, **unless** the options need rich rendering (icons, descriptions) → `Select`. More than 15 options, or search required: `Combobox`. Several values: `Checkbox` up to 5 options, `Combobox` in multiple mode beyond that. An on/off toggle that takes effect immediately: `Switch`.

Pick the surface from how much it blocks and how long its content is. A blocking decision (confirm, destroy): `AlertDialog`. A short task with no inner scrolling: `Dialog`. Long content or side context: `Sheet` from `md` up, `Drawer` below — **unless** it is side navigation, which stays a `Sheet` at every width (this is what `Sidebar` does below `md`). Anchored, non-blocking content with no scrolling and at most 3 fields: `Popover`. An informative preview on hover, from `md` up: `HoverCard`. A one-line, non-interactive label of at most 80 characters: `Tooltip`.

Pick how to present a collection from the nature of its content. Short-lived actions opened from a trigger: `DropdownMenuItem`. Rows to compare that share the same attributes, 3 or more per row: `Table`. A vertical list of entries (media, title, description, actions): `Item` inside an `ItemGroup`. A self-contained block with a header, body and footer, alone or in a grid: `Card`.
